texts: small diamond, humble
The diamond hides its brilliance in plain earth and asks for no throne; teach me to be that modest.
My friend is a genius with a diamond of a mind, yet he still touches the feet of every elder and thanks the cleaner by name.
Give me a verse about a person of rare worth who still bows low before everyone, who never mentions his gifts, and who receives respect precisely because he never asks for any.
doha on being a diamond but staying low and quiet?
need a humble doha with a heron and a musk deer in it
My teacher knows more than the whole faculty, yet he walks with eyes down like a heron wading softly, and never mentions the fragrance of his own fame like a musk deer.
heron, musk deer, humble
The heron stands proud and still, the musk deer carries sweetness unknowing; teach me to be small and unaware of my worth.
Write a doha on the meek who do not announce their gifts: the heron that stands patient and low, the musk deer that carries its perfume unseen, and the blessing that finds them in the end.
Bend like the clay on the potter's wheel, supple and unproud, and even the snake will pass you by.
Compose a verse on the person who yields like soft clay in the potter's hand, bows his head even to a snake in his path, and is shaped by grace into something worth keeping.
doha about bowing low like a snake slipping under clay?
snake, clay, bow low
My grandmother says her potter-and-clay life taught her to bend, not break, even when a snake of a neighbour spat his venom at her.
humble doha with sand and a door please
sand and doors, bow low
Write me a doha about the one who goes in through the lowest door, crouching as he enters, who walks gently on the sand and leaves no mark, and who is welcomed by all because he asked for nothing.
On the sand I leave no footprint, at the door I bend my head; so grace walks in beside the small.
When I visited the old man's hut I had to duck through the low door, and he smiled and said that was the best lesson he could give me, standing in his sandy yard.
The fish in the stream keeps low beneath the waves of pride, and the fire of ambition burns the loud while sparing the meek.
doha for staying humble with a fish and fire in it
Write a verse about the humble soul who is like a fish moving quietly through its water while others burn in the fire of their own ambition, and who ends up wiser, calmer, and loved.
After my promotion, my mentor, who once saved my job, took the lowest seat; the fish does not boast of the water, he said, and the fire of praise burns the careless.
fish, fire, stay small
My cousin always let others serve themselves first at the feast, and somehow the best portion ended up on his plate.
Lower than the lowest, softer than the softest, he bows, and grace leans down to meet him; sing his bowing.
quick doha on how the lowly always get blessed
meek, low, blessed

Please give me a verse about the quiet one who never pushes forward in a crowd, who lets others pass first and takes the last place at the table, and who is surprised when all the best blessings find him.
doha about being clay in the potter's hands please
When I began my apprenticeship, the old potter made me sit on the floor and knead the clay for a month, and I learned what bowing low really means.
Write a doha for the learner who admits he knows nothing, who lets the potter shape him like soft clay, and who is made into a worthy vessel because he never insisted on his own shape.
Let me be the clay that asks nothing of the potter's hand, yielding and humble, until it holds the wine of grace.
potter and clay, low
moneylender, moth, meekness
The moth bows to its beloved, the moneylender to his coin; one gives itself, one holds on, and only the first is free.
A moneylender in our lane, once harsh, now bows to the poorest customers and flutters like a moth around their blessings instead of their debts.
humble doha with a moneylender and a moth
Write a couplet about the moth who gives up its glow to the light and the moneylender who learns, too late, that bowing low would have earned more than any pile of coins ever could.
Make me a verse about a seeker who makes himself as small as a grain of sand, lets everyone walk over him without complaint, and in that smallness finds a freedom no proud person will ever taste.
Small as a grain of sand, I ask for nothing, and so I carry the whole shore within me.
At the village fair my uncle was pushed aside again and again and just kept smiling, shaking sand from his sandals, saying it is fine to be small.
doha on being small like sand pls
grain of sand, smallness
My nani sits at her spinning wheel with her head down and refuses every praise for her work, saying she only did what she was given to do.
spinning wheel, bowed head
can u write a humble doha with a spinning wheel
Round and round the spinning wheel hums its quiet song, and the spinner bends her head lower than her work.
Give me a verse about the woman at her spinning wheel who works all day with bowed head, never speaking of her skill, and whose fine yarn is praised by everyone except herself.
The green parrot does not call the song its own; it bows to every voice, and so it learns them all.
humble doha with a parrot in it?
My little sister loves her parrot, and she says it knows more than she does because it never argues, only listens and repeats.
parrot, humility
Compose a doha about the parrot that repeats whatever it hears and never claims any word as its own, and teach us how to speak only what we have received and how to bow before the giver of words.
humble doha with prayer beads and a rainbird
I want a doha about the quiet devotee turning prayer beads while a rainbird calls for the first drop, who seeks nothing for himself, bows his head to whatever falls, and is satisfied.
My grandmother counts her prayer beads each dawn while the rainbird calls from the roof, and she thanks the sky for whatever comes, even nothing.
The rainbird bows its beak to the sky and waits for a single drop; prayer beads slip through the fingers of the humble, who ask for nothing more.
rainbird, prayer beads, meek
Cast the net of your hope and then bow your head; the waters give what they give to those who ask without demand.
humble doha with a net in it pls
net, bowing low
Write a doha for the one who casts his net each day and accepts whatever comes, who never grumbles at the empty hours, and who is richer in spirit than the greedy man with a full catch.
The fisherman's net came up empty and he laughed, folded it neatly, and thanked the water anyway; I wish I could take my losses that humbly.
doha on being humble before people who know more

Write a verse about how the person who honestly admits he is small and still learning receives more wisdom than the person who pretends to know everything, and how the first one grows while the other stays fixed.
I started my first job as a trainee and decided to just keep quiet, listen, and bow to everyone's experience, and weirdly I learned faster than the loud ones.
bow before the wise
O humble heart, lower than the lowest, that is how the highest comes to dwell in you.
The mountain bows to nobody, but the humble man bows to even the pebble at its foot; sing which of the two is greater.
doha about a mountain of a man who still bows low?
mountain, bowing low
My professor is the biggest name in his field, a real mountain, yet he sits on the floor with the students and asks them what they think.
Write a couplet about a man tall as a mountain in learning and fame, who still lowers his head to everyone, speaks softly, and is loved more for his smallness than for his height.
Write a verse on how the humble do their work without wishing to be known, like a bridge that carries everyone across and asks for nothing, or a fish that gives without ever being thanked.
humble doha with a bridge and fish thx
The old man built a bridge over the stream and never signed his name; the fish know him better than the village does.
bridge, fish, quiet service
Lay yourself like a bridge beneath the feet of strangers, and be glad that even the fish never learn your name.
Lowest of the low, I bow, and the whole sky comes down to kiss my forehead.
My new neighbour never talks about himself; he just helps carry groceries and says he is only a visitor in everyone's life.
short doha on being the least of everyone
Give me a doha about the man who sits in the last row, listens when others speak, answers only when asked, and finds in his own silence the quiet joy that proud speakers never get to feel.
the lowly receive
yielding, soft, gentle
doha about saying sorry first and letting go
I fold my pride like a prayer shawl and set it down; how light the road becomes without it.
Please write a verse for the person who gives way in every quarrel, who says sorry even when he is not at fault, and who finds that this softness has made him the strongest voice in the family.
When the elders argued I stayed quiet, bowed, and apologised first even though I was right, and somehow the whole family felt lighter.
Compose a verse on how the one who bends at the right moment never breaks, who gives way when pushed and returns when the storm has passed, while the stiff and proud are the first to fall.
bow, give way
In the office fight over the credit, I just stepped back and said let them have it, and strangely the boss noticed me the most.
The reed bends before the gale and rises when it is gone; so the humble soul meets every storm of the world.
doha on the power of staying soft
My teacher walks as if he is afraid of crushing something; he has never raised his voice, and the whole class sits silent when he speaks.
doha for a humble person who never says a bad word?
Make me a doha about a gentle man who walks with downcast eyes, speaks softly, never compares himself with others, and is welcomed everywhere simply because he makes no demand on anyone.
Beautiful is the one who walks as if the road itself were holy, with eyes cast down and a quiet step.
soft step, lowered eyes
weaver's loom, humble
Write a verse on the weaver at his loom who works for hours with a bowed head, never seeking applause, and whose cloth warms the whole village while his name is forgotten and he is perfectly content.
The loom hums low, the weaver bows lower, and the cloth he makes covers a thousand backs.
doha about weaving humbly at the weaver's loom
My father worked at his loom for forty years and never once asked to be thanked, saying the cloth was thanks enough.
After my father lost his business he just smiled, bowed his head, and started working under his old employee without a word of complaint.
doha on living with open hands pls
humble guest in the world
A guest at the world's long table, I take the least and thank the host; that is my whole wealth.
Give me a verse for the person who understands that he is only a guest in this life, who lives with open hands, bows to everyone he meets, and is richer than any who tried to hold on to more.
doha on prayer beads and a crow, about staying humble
My uncle sits on the porch turning his prayer beads without a word, while a crow squawks on the wall, and I feel which of the two is closer to God.
The crow caws loudly while the prayer beads slip quietly through humble fingers; the loudest voice is not the nearest to the heavens.
Write me a verse about the one who counts his prayer beads in silence and does not mind the crow cawing at him, who bows his head and asks for nothing, and who is heard where it counts.
prayer beads, crow, humbly
humble doha with a river in it
Write a doha about the river that always flows to the lowest place, never climbing, never boasting, and is carried all the way to its journey's end because it was willing to go down.
My grandfather says to be like the river, always flowing lower, and he lived that way, helping every neighbour and never taking credit.
The river bends to every bank and bend, and so it arrives at last; teach me to bend like that.
river, low flowing
When my coworker shot a sharp remark at me, like an arrow, I did not answer, and a week later even the loud crow of an office manager respected my silence.
arrow, crow, meekness
doha about arrow and crow, humble version
The arrow flies straight and returns to the earth; the crow squawks and flies on; only the humble know where to rest.
Compose a doha on the humble soul who does not rise on his own noise like a crow, nor wound others with sharp words like an arrow, and who finds a quiet resting place wherever he lands.
humble doha with salt and a thief
salt, thief, owning nothing
The thief takes the coins and leaves the salt of tears; the humble, who owned nothing, lose nothing to any thief.
A thief came into our poor neighbour's room and found only salt; the neighbour offered him a meal anyway, smiling, bowing his head.
Please write a verse for the one who owns so little that no thief can steal from him, whose only treasure is a pinch of salt and a quiet mind, and who therefore sleeps without fear.
My friend who deals in gold in the market is the kindest man I know and treats the sweeper like family.
Among the shine of gold and the crowd's roar, he walks the market with lowered eyes, richer for what he does not claim.
gold, market, humbly

Give me a verse about a trader in the market who sells gold all day and still bows to every poor customer, knowing that his wealth is borrowed and that humility is the only coin that never loses value.
doha on staying humble even in the gold market
Softly, softly, as the dawn comes without trumpets, so the humble heart enters the room.
Please compose a verse about the person who wins great honour yet keeps his head low, who thanks his teachers and the unseen helpers, and who knows that every achievement was given, not made.
When my sister won the national prize, she took the first bus home and helped Mom wash the dishes as if nothing had happened.
doha on being humble in success, gimme something short
quiet, gentle, unassuming
doha on sand and humility pls
The old gardener walks on bare sand every morning to bless the ground, saying the lowest things carry the most.
The sand does not argue with the wave; it opens, and the wave leaves a gift of shells.

Please write me a verse about a person who remains small and soft, like fine sand under every foot, who never complains about being walked on and who in the end holds the water the proud cannot catch.
sand, bowing
I have adored a teacher from afar for years, like the chakor bird watching, and I never asked to be noticed, only to learn.
doha for a chakor bird with a humble heart
Write a doha about the devotee who, like the chakor bird, looks upward in love without demanding anything, content to bow and watch, certain that being allowed to love is already more than enough.
The chakor bird lifts its face to the distant silver and asks for nothing but to gaze; the humble love without a claim.
chakor bird, humble love
humble doha with a churn in it?
My aunt churns the butter at dawn with a bowed head, and she says the cream comes only when the one who churns forgets herself.
The churn turns slowly in humble hands, and cream rises for the one who asks for nothing.
Compose a verse about the woman who works the churn each morning in silence, bows her head to her labour, and receives the sweetest butter, as grace comes to the one who does not demand.
churn, patient and low
palanquin bearers, humbly
Humble shoulders carry the palanquin of kings, and the Lord rides with the ones who carry, not the carried.
Write a doha about the groom's palanquin bearers who carry the great on their shoulders, bow under the weight, and are in their lowliness closer to heaven than the one who rides upon them.
At the wedding I saw the bearers of the palanquin smiling as they lowered the groom, while he looked down at them as if they were his furniture.
humble doha with a palanquin pls
Last Friday in the mosque I saw the rich trader kneel beside the poor labourer, shoulder to shoulder, and neither one looked up.
In the mosque the brow touches the floor and the whole body becomes smaller than a speck of dust; there the proud heart learns to rest.
Give me a verse about the believer in the mosque who presses his forehead to the ground, lets go of every title he carries in the world, and rises up lighter, humbler, and closer to peace.
humble doha with a mosque thx
mosque, low bow
doha about a yogi who has no pride
The yogi who lives by our village could do wonders, yet he sweeps the path each morning and insists he is only the servant of those who come.
Write a doha about a yogi who has mastered breath and mind but still sits at the back, eats last, and speaks like a student, because he knows the one who says "I know" has forgotten.
yogi, no claims
The yogi's mastery shows only as a deeper bow; the more he holds, the lower he leans.

Write me a doha about the pious man who put aside his forehead mark and title, sat among the poor on the floor, and felt for the first time the fruit of being nothing, while the cleric watched with tears.
humble doha with forehead mark and cleric
My uncle wiped off his forehead mark and sat down beside the cleric on the floor, saying that for tonight they were both just guests.
A forehead mark shows who you are, but the bowed head hides who you are; the cleric and the guest meet in that hiding.
forehead mark, cleric, humbled
doha about bowing even to your enemy
bow to everyone
Please write a doha about the one who bows to everyone he meets without choosing, who sees no one as lesser, and who finds that even his enemy becomes gentle in the presence of such a quiet greeting.
I touched the feet of the man who insulted me last year and I think that was the best thing I ever did.
I bow to the wise and the foolish, the friend and the foe, for each is a face of the One; sing this bowing.
doha about a student who stays teachable
Give me a verse about the student who walks into the master's room with a bowed head and an empty cup, who does not interrupt, and who is filled with more than he ever dared to hope for.
A cup held low in two cupped hands is the first to be filled; humble one, hold your hands low.
On my first day at the workshop I said I knew nothing, and the master smiled and said that is the only student I can teach.
empty cup, learner
Our small house has a very low entrance and my grandfather says this is on purpose so that everybody who visits learns to bow.
A house with a low doorway teaches all who enter to bow their heads; there the blessing is always home.
humble house, low roof
humble doha with a house in it
Compose a verse for the family that lives in a modest house with a low roof, where every guest bows entering and every host bows welcoming, and where more love lives than in any hall of pride.

Write me a verse about how the proud burn like a fire that wants to rise and consume everything, while the humble are like quiet embers that keep the household warm through the long night without a word.
My uncle's rage burned bright and left everything black, but my aunt's quiet patience warmed the family for forty years like a banked fire.
fire, softness
doha on being soft like fire's smoke?
The great fire roars and is soon spent, but the small ember glows through the night; be the ember.
One cloth sheet between two, and the poorer one bows as though he were the one receiving.
My grandfather had one blanket-like cloth sheet and spread it for a stranger, then thanked the stranger for letting him help.
doha about the cloth sheet that the humble man shares
Compose a doha on the poor man who has only one cloth sheet and still offers half of it to the stranger shivering outside, bowing with thanks that someone has given him a chance to give.
cloth sheet, giving
Make me a doha about the person who lets everyone else eat before him, who says he is not hungry when there is not enough, and whose emptiness is more filled with joy than any feast.
doha on putting others before yourself
Last at the table, first in the heart, he serves with downcast eyes and no thought of his own.
At every family gathering my mother eats last, standing in the kitchen, and when I ask her why she says that is where she is happiest.
service, last place
My father, a hard-driving boss like a lion at work, wears a plain cloth sheet to prayers and sits at the back without anyone's knowing him.
lion, cloth sheet, humbled
Write a verse about the powerful man who walks like a lion in the world but takes off his pride like a cloth sheet when he prays and enters as the smallest child of God.
The lion may roar from the hill, but the humble man, small as a cloth sheet folded in a corner, passes through every gathering unchallenged.
humble doha with a lion and a cloth sheet thanks
bee, humble taking
The bee bows to every blossom and robs none of its beauty; humble labour makes the sweetest honey.
Write a doha about the humble worker who, like the bee, takes only a little from each flower, gives life in return, never boasts of the honey, and leaves the garden richer for his visit.
The honey bee never claims the flower; she bows, takes a little, and leaves it more beautiful, which is how I want to treat people.
doha on a bee that bows to flowers
At the old mosque I watched a leaf blow in and settle by the last row, exactly where the humble old man always sat.
humble doha with leaf and mosque
leaf and mosque, humble
Please give me a doha about the worshipper who enters the mosque like a falling leaf, without announcement, lays his claims down, and sits at the edge, grateful to be part of the gathering.
A leaf falls without a sound near the mosque; so the humble soul comes to the sacred place with no claim.
The snake-charmer in our town bows to his snake every day before the show and says the snake is the real master.
doha about bowing before the snake
Compose a verse for the one who bows before even the most dangerous snake, because he knows pride is the venom he carries and that humility is the only antidote to it.
The snake raises its hood to the proud and lowers it to the one who bows; sing the gentle power of yielding.
snake, bowing, peace
credit to others
After the project won the award, our team lead called all of us to the stage and stood in the back row himself.

Please write a verse about the gifted person who is asked how he accomplished so much, and answers that he did nothing, that it all came through him, and that he is only grateful to have been a channel.
I did nothing; it was done through me; I only stood aside, and the work was finished.
doha on giving all the credit away?
Give me a verse about the person who lays himself down like a bridge so others may cross, who is walked over by the whole town and does not mind, and who is the true carrier of the world.
In our village the old man laid a plank bridge over the mud every monsoon so that the children could cross and never wanted to be thanked.
bridge, selfless low
doha on being a bridge for others
Be the bridge beneath the feet, not the tower above the town; the humble never fear a fall.
When my boss shouted like a drawn sword, my colleague answered with a quiet apology, like morning dew, and the shouting stopped.
humble doha with dew and a sword
Write a couplet on the gentle person who is like the morning dew, small and unprotected, who bows to even the sword of the proud, and whose softness blunts every blade raised against him.
The dew bows to the blade of grass and the sword is blunted by the humble heart that does not resist.
dew, sword, meek
humble doha with a door
door, bow in
My grandfather always touched the threshold before entering any door and said you must ask the place for permission to be a guest.
Bend your head at the doorway and the whole world opens to you; the low gate is the widest gate.
Please write a doha about the one who enters every door with a bowed head, who greets the porter and the king alike, and who is welcomed by every family because his humility asks for nothing.
Write a verse about the humble trader at the crossroads who bows to rich and poor alike, who never haggles with pride, and who is remembered when the whole market has forgotten the clever men.
At the crossroads where all paths meet, the market roars, and the humble stand with folded hands and let the world pass.
crossroads market, humble
humble doha with crossroads and market pls
At the crossroads market the old cobbler greets every passer-by with folded hands, whether they buy or not, and everyone loves him.
